Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the final session on Day 3 and the start of the Windies' first innings as well. The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of South Africa who slowly stride out and take their places on the field. It will be captain Kraigg Brathwaite to open the innings for West Indies alongside Mikyle Louis. Kagiso Rabada, just 5 wickets away from the landmark of 300 Test wickets has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Right then! As West Indies prepare to embark on their first innings, the question lingers in the air - can they dig out a big first innings lead, or will the South African bowling unit rise to the challenge? The stage is set for a riveting second innings, where every run and wicket will shape the narrative of this encounter. Stick around as the final session is up next.

On the other hand, West Indies kept up nipping the deliveries in and out, keeping the Proteas batters under pressure from the first over of the inning. The two youngest seamers, Jayden Seales and Shamar Joseph were outstanding with their job. Shamar Joseph, the local boy, picked up a five-fer but had to walk out of the park because of cramps. Jayden Seales supported him and picked three wickets from the other end. Jason Holder has also chipped in for one hunting Tristan Stubbs off the pitch in the first session. The spin attacks were not that fruitful for the Windies at the start but Gudakesh Motie helped his team to take the last breakthrough which made the bowlers sweat.

After the Lunch break, nothing much changed for South Africa as things kept falling apart. From the 29th to the 31st over they lost three of their batters. Kyle Verreynne on the other side of the pitch tried to hold the wicket as he was the only shining hope for the Proteas fans, but soon the hope was as well blown away. The last two men on the pitch did exceptionally well to sustain long enough and keep the scoreboard ticking. No one expected them to bat that long but this is why we all love this sport. They had the longest partnership in the inning, scoring 63 runs in 107 deliveries. The second session was well was extended for 30 minutes, which resulted in the end of the first inning. Once again, kudos to the tail-enders as it's because of them South Africa were able to post 160 runs on the board.

Day 1, Tea break! 28 overs in the second session and it was an extended one that saw 6 wickets fall for 96 runs. What a session though and West Indies could have and should have bundled out the Proteas for about 100 runs but what a stand from Dane Piedt and Nandre Burger and they have given the bowlers something to bowl at.

OUT! LBW! And that's it! Gudakesh Motie wraps up things and gets his first wicket. But, this 63-run stand really made the West Indies work a bit more hard. Gudakesh Motie stays around the pegs and drops it in the corridor of the middle and leg stump line, with a hint of turn into the batter. Nandre Burger goes back and across to work it to the leg side but plays over the line of the ball. It sneaks past the inside edge and wears on his back pad. The umpire raises the finger on the appeal for LBW, and Nandre Burger sends it upstairs. Nothing on UltraEdge and Ball Tracking shows three reds as the ball is crashing into the middle and leg stump on the projection. Of what looked like a below triple-figure score, South Africa have well-managed to put on vital runs on the board with this 10th wicket stand, but it is still well below the 1st inning par score at this venue.

Right then, West Indies would be mighty pleased with their bowling efforts and would like to reflect those in the coming two sessions of Day 1. However, the second session is considered as the best time to bat in Test cricket and South Africa would need to build a strong healthy partnership to ensure that the game doesn't slip too far away. With David Bedingham trying to weather the storm, he needs good support from the other end. Stick around as the post-Lunch session is up next shortly. Play resumes at 10.10 pm IST (1640 GMT).

South Africa found themselves in an early spot of bother as their top order including de Zorzi, Markram and Bavuma were blown away in a flash. However, Tristan Stubbs, though crawled, displayed a nice temperament and negotiated the dual swing and bounce watchfully for most of the part. David Bedingham provided good support and has navigated with caution until now. Just when the partnership was blossoming well in resilience, Tristan Stubbs lost his wicket minutes before the end of the session compelling South Africa to build up once again.

Jayden Seales provided that early breakthrough for the West Indies and opened the game right on. But, it was the local boy, Shamar Joseph who ran a riot through and dismantled the batters with a couple of wickets to his name. He bowled a pulsating spell with a searing pace and didn't let the South African batters get off pressure. The others too, kept the batters in check with their tight lines and lengths with Jason Holder eventually getting one to his name as well.

The first session has highlighted the typical challenges of day one in Test cricket. The ball's movement off the seam in both directions has made batting difficult, requiring constant adjustment from the batters. While four wickets have fallen, it's the numerous plays and misses that truly indicate that the bowlers have found a consistent line and length. South Africa would have lost a couple of more wickets had those catches been not grassed. But overall, the West Indian bowling was well-disciplined almost for the whole session.

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the formalities and it is now time to play. The two umpires have taken their positions on the field and so have the players of West Indies. It will be the pair of Aiden Markram and Tony de Zorzi that will open the innings for South Africa. Jason Holder will take the new ball and is raring to go. Three slips in place, let's play...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of the game but first, the two sets of players line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of South Africa followed by the national anthem of West Indies.

PITCH REPORT - Daren Ganga is pitchside. He says that it is pitch number 4 and it is a bit cloudy and the boundaries are pretty even on either side of the deck. Vernon Philander joins him and says that the surface is pretty exciting as there is a good grass covering and will aid stroke-making and there will be some swing early on with the spinners coming into play later on.

Kraigg Brathwaite, the captain of West Indies says that they would have batted first as well and it looks like a good deck. Informs that Shamar Joseph is in for Kemar Roach as the pitch could slow down and they want some extra pace. Adds that Alick Athanaze batted well and it's all about reimagining your game plan.

Temba Bavuma, the skipper of South Africa wins the toss and elected to bat first. He says that it looks like a good wicket to bat on. They would like to put pressure on the opposition and capitalize on that. He continues that it's an important game like the other matches and they would win the series at the Caribbean. Ends up saying they have two changes, Dane Piedt and Nandre Burger are in for Ryan Rickelton and Lungi Ngidi.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Kraigg Brathwaite (C), Mikyle Louis, Keacy Carty, Alick Athanaze, Kavem Hodge, Jason Holder, Joshua Da Silva (WK), Gudakesh Motie, Jomel Warrican, Shamar Joseph (In for Kemar Roach), Jayden Seales.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Aiden Markram, Tony de Zorzi, Tristan Stubbs, Temba Bavuma (C), David Bedingham, Kyle Verreynne (WK), Wiaan Mulder, Keshav Maharaj, Dane Piedt (In for Ryan Rickelton), Kagiso Rabada, Nandre Burger (In for Lungi Ngidi).
TOSS - South Africa won the toss and they have elected to BAT first.

After losing plenty of overs in what could have been an epic encounter, the players and the fans will be glad to know that the weather in Guyana over the next five days is much better and we should get plenty of cricketing action. Toss is always a big factor in Test matches, so, stay tuned as toss and teams sheets are up in a bit.

West Indies on the other hand will be a bit thankful to the rain Gods as they didn't have a good outing with the bat in the first innings but did more than enough in the final innings. A lot of 30s throughout the lineup but only Alick Athanaze managed to score a valuable 92 in the final innings of the Test match which the hosts would want to rectify. Also, Shamar Joseph is all set to make his home Test debut it seems as the Windies look to tighten things up with the ball.

South Africa comes into this game having played some solid cricket in the first Test match but they weren't at their fluid best and would want to walk away with a series victory. Aiden Markram surprisingly played his first drawn Test having either won or lost all of his previous matches. Skipper, Temba Bavuma would want the same solidity from the middle order and maybe a bit more from the top order and we might just see Nandre Burger getting a game as well.

Hello and a warm welcome to the Providence Stadium in Guyana as West Indies host South Africa for the 2nd and final Test match of the series. After a fascinating draw in Port of Spain, the visiting Proteas team will be hoping that this time rain doesn't stand in the way and the hosts will be eyeing a similar sort of gritty performance that earned them a draw in the first game.
